chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: Paying for Lincoln: knickers and the dormitory
summary: The family could not easily afford Lincoln, and the state paid nothing. Thomas talks about wearing short pants and living in the campus dormitory.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, now how did they arrange for you to go there?

Damn if I know. It was money, of course. It was money they couldn't afford and I guess they had gone to see Mr. Sims to get registration and all those things together but the state had nothing to do with it. You know, the State of Missouri had nothing to do with it, I mean, so far as footing the bill of expenses. You go, I mean we say you go or you pay. You know that's the score there. So, in going to, they gave me the go sign. Well, fortunately during that summer I don't know if you've ever seen short pants.
Gee, I can't remember them.
You're an Englishman, you might call them knickers.
Oh, yeah, thats right. They wore them here?
Yeah.
They never wore them in England much.
I had to wear them, man.
Because I remember a cousin of mine coming from Canada and we thought that was the funniest thing we'd ever seen.
JTHOMAS (1) 15
Of course, they used to wear them in England but they'd gone out.

Well, what happened, too, I think, in fact I know now, you don't want a kid to grow up too fast. Let him grow up with respect, you know, which I don't think that had anything to with it, the short pants, but that was their thought.
Now, where are we now?
Well, you're going off to Lincoln? But, you've got to board there. Who were you going to stay with?

Well, here's what happened for me, Stan. During that summer I had a couple of good buddies and we used to go around and look for work. But I must tell you this, I might have my time a little mixed up, yeah I think it's a little early for this. Well, anyway, in the first place you stay in a dormitory.
Well, that was what I was really getting at because that would add to the expense, wouldn't it?
All the way. And there's food.
I thought maybe you had an aunt or something like that.
No. Stayed on the campus.
Well, that was very good for you in a way.
Now as I see it, I think it's one of the finest things that ever happened to me. That's the way I feel about it.
